qualification: Deliberately irregular, nonconforming FFV1 timestamp order [0,40ms,20ms]. This is recovery consistency for already accepted input, not a Matroska conformance claim. RFC 9559 section 10 requires a past-timestamp frame to reference a known frame.
Each original FFV1 keyframe independently decodes to its authored distinct pixels; ordered and irregular files contain the same three decoded frames.
Full export previously accepted and sorted all frames. Before the fix, [0,30ms) trimming silently dropped the later stored 20ms frame. The fix retains both selected frames.
Exact trim boundaries and nonzero starts match ordered controls; packet count limits still reject excess work without publishing a partial output.
Software decoding/export qualification; no hardware playback or performance claim.
counting: One robustness problem: preserve already recoverable frames consistently during trimming. Fixture generation, controls and resource checks are not separate IDs.
